transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi! ConversalQ developer support here. What can I help you with?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.text: I'm integrating your REST API into our Node.js app. I keep getting 401 errors even though I'm passing my API key in the header.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Let's take a look. Can you share how you're sending the API key in the request header?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's the right format. A few things to check: 1) Make sure there are no extra spaces in the key, 2) Verify you're using the API key from the Developer section, not the account password. Can you confirm which key you're using?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.text: I'm using the one under Settings > API Keys. Let me double-check for spaces... actually there's a trailing newline! My code was reading from a .env file.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's a very common issue! In Node.js, you can trim it with: process.env.API_KEY.trim(). Try that and let me know if it resolves it.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.text: One second... Yes! That fixed it. I'm getting 200 responses now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent! For future reference, always .trim() your environment variables when reading API keys. Is there anything else about the API integration I can help with?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.text: Actually yes — what's the rate limit for the /chat endpoint?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: On the Pro plan you're on, it's 60 requests per minute per API key. You'll receive a 429 response if exceeded, with a Retry-After header telling you how long to wait.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.text: Perfect. Thanks for the quick help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Happy to help! Good luck with the integration.
